findings.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of || when combining isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner checks, making the condition effectively always false and denying legitimate team admins/owners from adding guests

Calendar sync uses the requester's own credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's credentials (booking.user.credentials), causing calendar updates to fail silently or update the wrong calendar when a non-organizer attendee adds a guest

Server-side schema (ZAddGuestsInputSchema) does not validate uniqueness of guest emails in the submitted array, relying only on a client-side refine() check, allowing duplicate attendee rows if the dialog is bypassed
Neither the 'Add guests' menu item nor the addGuests handler checks booking status before allowing guests to be added, permitting guests to be added to cancelled or past bookings
Duplicate-guest detection is a read-then-write check with no DB-level uniqueness constraint or transaction, allowing race conditions where concurrent addGuests calls insert duplicate attendee rows

Duplicate-guest and blacklist email comparisons are case-sensitive for the incoming guest email while the blacklist is lowercased, causing case-mismatched duplicates or blacklisted emails to bypass detection
Email subject in organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses attendees[0].name instead of the newly added guest's name, producing a misleading subject line
Email send failures in the addGuests handler are only console.log'd instead of using structured logging/alerting, making failed notifications invisible in production

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar sync uses the requester's own credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's credentials (booking.user.credentials), causing calendar updates to fail silently or update the wrong calendar when a non-organizer attendee adds a guest

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` is sufficient to pass the permission check). However, when syncing calendar attendees it builds the `EventManager` using the authenticated requester (`...user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The booking organizer’s credentials are available in the fetched booking (`include: { user: { include: { credentials: true }}}`) but are not used. This means an attendee adding guests will attempt to update calendars using the attendee’s integrations rather than the organizer’s, which can update the wrong calendar or fail if the attendee has no calendar credentials—this is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side schema (ZAddGuestsInputSchema) does not validate uniqueness of guest emails in the submitted array, relying only on a client-side refine() check, allowing duplicate attendee rows if the dialog is bypassed
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the server does not enforce/deduplicate unique guest emails within the submitted input, so repeated emails can pass through and result in duplicate attendee rows being inserted (e.g., via createMany).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Neither the 'Add guests' menu item nor the addGuests handler checks booking status before allowing guests to be added, permitting guests to be added to cancelled or past bookings

adjudication.rationale: The new UI action is always added to `bookingOptions` without any conditional logic around `booking` state/time. On the server, `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking by `id` and then unconditionally updates `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` after only checking permissions; it does not check any booking state (e.g., canceled) nor does it check `booking.startTime/endTime` against the current time to prevent adding guests to past bookings. Therefore, as written, guests can be added to any accessible booking regardless of whether it is in the past or otherwise inactive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-guest detection is a read-then-write check with no DB-level uniqueness constraint or transaction, allowing race conditions where concurrent addGuests calls insert duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: The handler does perform a non-atomic read-then-write check (it reads existing attendees via `findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`, computes `uniqueGuests`, then later does `booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})`), so concurrent calls could bypass the in-memory duplicate filtering. However, the proposed finding specifically claims there is "no DB-level uniqueness constraint or transaction" and that duplicates will be inserted. The diff does not show the Prisma schema / DB constraints for attendees (e.g., a unique index on `(bookingId, email)`), nor any `skipDuplicates` or explicit transaction usage. Without seeing the DB constraints, it is not verifiable from this diff that duplicates can actually be inserted (a DB constraint could instead cause one call to fail).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email subject in organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses attendees[0].name instead of the newly added guest's name, producing a misleading subject line

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject is built with `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. The diff does not establish that the subject is intended to reference the newly added guest(s); it may be intended to reference the primary attendee/booker (often stored as the first attendee), which is consistent with many booking-related email subjects. Additionally, newly added guests are created with `name: ""` in `addGuests.handler.ts`, so even if the intent were to use a newly added guest's name, that data is not available from this diff. Thus the claim that this is a definite misleading bug is not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures in the addGuests handler are only console.log'd instead of using structured logging/alerting, making failed notifications invisible in production

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email notification send is wrapped in a try/catch that swallows all errors and only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` (no error object, no rethrow). The handler still returns success (`{ message: "Guests added" }`) even if emails fail, making notification failures effectively silent/non-actionable in production unless console output is monitored. This is directly verifiable in the diff.
